integrity: The proof reduces one unit vector by dihedral symmetry to a reference edge and determines the sign of the isosceles chord difference on each of the eight relative edge classes. Only the two quarter-turn edge families survive, including their shared endpoints. An exact Q(sqrt(2)) checker replays the edge identities and equality chords; the finite grid is supplementary to the analytic continuum proof. No independent audit or independent validation has been performed.
scientific_limitations: The classification concerns unit vectors in the regular-octagonal plane only. It does not classify non-unit isosceles orthogonality or assert an analogous rigidity theorem for all regular polygons.
title: Rigid unit isosceles orthogonality in the regular octagon
